_about: Per-name one-pager justifications for the report appendix. Keyed by ticker. make_report.py renders a page for every ranked ticker; scores come from the scoring data, text from here. Fields: company, words, read, long, c1..c6 (justification per criterion), flags (list), thin (true if reconstructed from the full text because stored notes were thin).

CCOI.long: Author states he is buying ("So why am I buying?"); no formal disclosure line
CCOI.c1: Partial (0.5). The core IP-transit business is steady and cheap, and the Sprint wireline network is being refilled with Wavelengths and IPv4 leasing. The article frames it mainly as undervalued hard assets plus a recovery, not a long secular growth story.
CCOI.c2: Full. Base case $81/share vs about $12.22 at the publish-day close (author range $40-150). No timeframe given, so the default 2 years applies, which is well above 40%/yr.
CCOI.c3: Full. Founder-CEO Dave Schaeffer is quoted saying he owns about 10% of the company. He has been selling, and the article says so.
CCOI.c4: Moderate (0.75). Scale and cost advantage: the lowest-cost transit network ($0.07/Mbps), owned fiber and data-center footprint, about 12.5M IPv4 addresses (cited in a related article; the author values the Sprint block via appraisals), and a proven founder-operator. Main threat: Wavelengths has repeatedly missed guidance, and the moat sits under a 7.4x-levered balance sheet.
CCOI.c5: Full. The market prices in a 98% dividend cut, founder selling, 16% short interest and an 86% drawdown. The author argues the core is intact and the hard assets cover the downside, so de-levering should force a re-rating.
CCOI.c6: Full. The $750M senior unsecured notes due June 15, 2027 are to be refinanced with 2033 secured notes, and leverage is guided to about 3x by May 2028.
flags: About 7.4x net leverage and a June 2027 maturity: refinancing risk.
Management has missed several Sprint and Wavelengths projections; the author expects the 2028 targets to be missed.
Founder selling and a 98% dividend cut. Fact-check: these are stated by the author and match filings.
Stock has fallen about 30% since publication (as of Oct 13).

HROW.long: Counted as long by the earlier manual check; no disclosure line was found in the saved text, so this needs re-checking
HROW.c1: Full. A branded ophthalmic portfolio (VEVYE at 42% of revenue, IHEEZO, TRIESENCE, plus the TYRVAYA acquisition) is growing; branded revenue rose 33% YoY to 79% of the total.
HROW.c2: Full. The author sees "a credible path" to $100 by 2028 vs $38.87 at the publish-day close: about 2.6x in about 2.4 years, roughly 50%/yr.
HROW.c3: Full per the stored score (CEO Mark Baum). The saved article doesn't give his stake, so this can't be confirmed from the text.
HROW.c4: Moderate (0.75). Edge rather than structural moat: a commercial ophthalmology platform that buys under-managed branded drugs (TYRVAYA from Viatris) and re-launches them through its own enlarged sales force, with >90% gross margin on IHEEZO. Main threat: execution. Management keeps missing its own guidance, and the author calls Baum a salesman.
HROW.c5: Partial (0.5). An earnings-review update: the author argues expectations have reset below guidance and H2 conversion isn't priced in, but gives no sharp reason the market is wrong beyond that.
HROW.c6: Full. Dated catalysts: IHEEZO's ~25% net price increase from July 1, 2026, VEVYE's new top-three PBM coverage from Aug 1, and the G-MELT NDA plus product catalysts in 2027.
flags: $300M of 8.625% notes due September 2030.
Guidance record is poor: Q2 revenue came in below the bottom of the range, again.
H2 2026 guide needs more than double H1 revenue.
Stock has fallen about 27% since publication (as of Oct 13).

PDEX.long: "I hold a position in the securities discussed"
PDEX.c1: Full. A profitable, self-funding maker of powered surgical handpieces whose orthopedic and robotic end-effector business rides growth in surgical robotics.
PDEX.c2: Partial (0.5). Base case about $100 vs $58.40 at the publish-day close: about +71% over the default 2 years, roughly 31%/yr (in the 25-40% band).
PDEX.c3: Partial (0.5). CEO Rick Van Kirk owns about 2.8%. Chairman Nicholas Swenson holds about 32%, but he isn't the CEO.
PDEX.c4: Strong (1). Switching costs plus intangibles: patented adaptive torque-limiting algorithms, characterized to each customer's own screw set, so a rival can't drop in a substitute. More than 15 years of patents back this up (e.g., DePuy's MatrixPRO II runs on it). Main threat: 79% customer concentration, likely Stryker, which has in-house capability.
PDEX.c5: Full. Headline EPS is inflated by a one-time Monogram gain and the stock is discounted for concentration. The author argues the core alone pays for the price, so the robotics option comes free; the customer's extension to 2028 with minimum volumes reduces the overhang.
PDEX.c6: Full. The robotics/Mako-related option reaches "a genuine catalyst in early 2027", per the author.
flags: One customer was 79% of 9-month FY26 revenue; the top three were 94%.
The chairman's stock is partly pledged against a loan, and the CEO has been trimming.
Some information comes from a management meeting, not filings (the author flags this).

BDC.long: "The author of this post holds a long position in BDC"
BDC.c1: Full. Industrial and enterprise networking for the AI, automation, Wi-Fi 7 and broadband (BEAD) build-outs. Solutions mix is targeted to reach 30% of revenue by 2028.
BDC.c2: Full. Base-case target $235 within two years vs $118.44 at the publish-day close: about +98%, roughly 41%/yr.
BDC.c3: Zero. CEO Ashish Chand is a long-time insider, but the article only cites a 6x-salary ownership requirement, not a large stake.
BDC.c4: Moderate (0.75). Switching costs and specification power: in industrial automation downtime is costly and rewiring is painful, plus channel and application-engineering breadth across a fragmented market. Main threat: larger networking players in the active layer it is now entering with RUCKUS.
BDC.c5: Full. The market fixes on RUCKUS's ~13x headline multiple and the leverage step-up. The author argues it lifts margins and mix, and that consensus for 2027-28 is stale, so revisions should re-rate the stock.
BDC.c6: Full. RUCKUS fully integrated by 2027, with most of the margin step-up in 2027, and management's 2.9x net-leverage target by 2027.
flags: $1.85B of new acquisition debt (JPM, SOFR+225); M&A and buybacks paused until leverage falls.
Stock has fallen about 8% since publication (as of Oct 13).

REAL.long: "The author of this post holds a long position in the stock discussed"
REAL.c1: Full. Leader in authenticated luxury resale, with a growing pre-owned watch and jewelry mix (a $35.7B market cited at a 13% CAGR) and AI-driven intake (Athena).
REAL.c2: Full. Base-case $19.22 (3.0x FY27E revenue) vs $11.66 at the publish-day close: +65%. Read as a valuation at the end of FY27 (about 1.4 years), that's about 40%/yr. On a 2-year reading it would be about 29%/yr and only 0.5.
REAL.c3: Zero. CEO Rati Sahi Levesque is a 15-year veteran, appointed in 2024; no large stake is stated.
REAL.c4: Narrow (0.5). Scale and trust in authentication (intake and authentication centers, data, brand) give a modest edge. Main threat: other resale marketplaces and the low switching costs of consignors.
REAL.c5: Full. The stock was punished for flat Q2 guidance and tough H2 comps. The author argues operating leverage (AEBITDA margin 7% to a 15-20% target) and FCF inflection aren't priced.
REAL.c6: Full per the stored score. Athena is targeted at ~50% of units by end-2026 and FY27 margins are the test; these are dated milestones rather than one hard event.
flags: Net leverage about 5.0x LTM; cash fell to $123.9M from $151.2M.
The author's model assumes ~12% more diluted shares vs FY25.
Stock has fallen about 16% since publication (as of Oct 13).

KITS.TO.long: "I have owned shares of KITS ... for a few months now"
KITS.TO.c1: Full. Online prescription eyewear is still early in penetration, and KITS is growing quickly against a high-markup incumbent chain.
KITS.TO.c2: Zero. No price target. The base scenario is about C$30.59 by FY2030 vs ~C$16.90 at the publish-day close: +84% over five years, roughly 13%/yr.
KITS.TO.c3: Full. Founder-CEO Roger Hardy holds about 20%+ per the stored note, and has been buying on the open market. The exact figure wasn't re-confirmed in the saved text.
KITS.TO.c4: Moderate (0.75). Cost advantage from vertical integration: its own Vancouver lab makes glasses at a fraction of incumbent cost, plus proprietary OpticianAI data and about 64% repeat revenue. The author rates the moat "middle of the pack". Edge: Hardy built and sold the same model (Coastal Contacts) once before. Main threat: EssilorLuxottica and Warby Parker.
KITS.TO.c5: Full. The headline multiple looks expensive because nearly all operating profit is reinvested in customer acquisition. The author argues steady-state earnings are much higher.
KITS.TO.c6: Partial (0.5). No dated catalyst; the case is a five-year compounding path.
flags: Modest dilution from stock-based pay assumed (34M to 35M shares).
Low current net margin because of heavy reinvestment.

LEAT.long: "Why I Own It: I bought this in early June 2026 at $12.00"
LEAT.c1: Full. A protective-gear brand (neck braces, helmets, body armor) taking share while the industry recovers from destocking. Revenue is still about 19% below its peak and margins are a third of peak.
LEAT.c2: Partial (0.5). Weighted fair value of about $22 vs $12.65 at the first close after publication: +74% (the author says +84% from $12.10) over the default 2 years, roughly 32-36%/yr.
LEAT.c3: Partial (0.5) per the stored score. Founder Dr. Christopher Leatt is Chairman and head of R&D; CEO Sean Macdonald's stake isn't stated in the article, so this can't be confirmed.
LEAT.c4: Moderate (0.75). Brand and IP: the original neck-brace inventor, with an ecosystem that customers buy for protection per dollar. Edge: growing about 27% while peers (Fox, Shimano) shrink. Main threat: a discretionary category and cyclical destocking.
LEAT.c5: Full. No analyst coverage; the discount is illiquidity, not a broken business, and the $1.30 EPS rests on management's own operating-leverage guidance.
LEAT.c6: Partial (0.5). Catalysts are quarterly margin expansion and a late-summer 2026 helmet launch; no hard dated re-rating event.
flags: Clean: $16.7M net cash, no debt, flat share count for a decade.
OTCQB-listed and illiquid.
Comparisons are getting harder (Q2 2026 laps +61%).

LUMN.long: "Note: the author holds a long position in the security analyzed"
LUMN.c1: Full. AI and cloud demand turns its 340,000-route-mile intercity fiber network into scarce infrastructure; Strategic revenue is over 50% of Business revenue, and digital and NaaS are growing about 36%.
LUMN.c2: Full. Base case about $17 (8x 2029 cash EBITDA) vs $7.96 at the publish-day close: +114%, about 46%/yr over the default 2 years (upside case $25-44).
LUMN.c3: Zero. The article gives no meaningful CEO stake.
LUMN.c4: Moderate (0.75). Hard-to-replicate assets: the Level 3 long-haul fiber, the largest US 400G footprint, and partnerships (AWS, Palantir, Corning). Main threat: Zayo competition for new builds, and future PCF deals may need costlier new conduit.
LUMN.c5: Full. The market still extrapolates telecom decline, while the mix has crossed to growth. The author argues EBITDA inflects in 2026, revenue in 2028, and the complexity and distress discount unwinds.
LUMN.c6: Partial (0.5). Catalysts (EBITDA inflection in 2026, Business revenue in 2028, further PCF wins) are described as "identifiable over the medium-term", not one dated event.
flags: Heavy debt, though net leverage fell below 4x after the FTTH sale, and Level 3 maturities run past 2030.
Stock has fallen about 37% since publication (as of Oct 13).

SRI.long: "Note: author holds a long position in the security analyzed"
SRI.c1: Full. MirrorEye camera-mirror systems (~1/4 of FY26 sales, ~100% North American share) on top of a cyclical recovery in Class 8 trucks, after selling legacy Control Devices.
SRI.c2: Full. Value about $15/share vs $7.28 at the publish-day close: +106%, about 43%/yr over the default 2 years.
SRI.c3: Zero. A new CEO (previously head of Electronics); no stake is stated.
SRI.c4: Moderate (0.75). Switching costs: MirrorEye is "spec-ed in" at OEMs (Daimler and Volvo programs ramping), with a near-monopoly in North America. Main threat: limited EU share gains against Bosch/MEKRA, and OEM validation cycles.
SRI.c5: Full. Orphaned by the market (down more than 60%, almost no coverage) because of a truck down-cycle. The author argues normalized earnings plus MirrorEye growth are mispriced.
SRI.c6: Partial (0.5). The author calls it "a patience story rather than one with a hard catalyst"; the credit facility refinancing (matures July 2027) is the nearest dated event.
flags: Thin covenant room (max 4x leverage, 2.5x interest coverage) could be breached if EBITDA falls further.
CEO and CFO turnover.
2026 EBITDA guide cut from $70M to $20-25M.
Stock has fallen about 16% since publication (as of Oct 13).

SUM.V.long: "Disclaimer: I am long shares at CAD$ 1.36"
SUM.V.c1: Full. A royalty model with high margins; the book moves from small cash flows to >$15M FCF in 2027 as Copperstone and Pitangui start production.
SUM.V.c2: Zero per the stored score: there's no explicit dated price target. The author's FCF math (15x 2027 FCF, about $2.10/share) implies about +41% from C$1.49, but it isn't stated as a target with a timeframe.
SUM.V.c3: Partial (0.5). Insiders own about 11% (company deck); CEO Drew Clark's personal stake isn't broken out.
SUM.V.c4: Narrow (0.5). Edge rather than moat: CEO Drew Clark comes from Metalla's growth years, and royalties are a structurally high-margin model. Main threat: execution and dilution at a small royalty company.
SUM.V.c5: Full. It trades at about 0.6x P/NAV vs peers above 1x; the author argues FCF arriving in 2027 closes that gap.
SUM.V.c6: Full. Copperstone and Pitangui production in mid/H2 2027, a PEA in H2 2026, and the silver-stream deficit settling in December 2027.
flags: History of equity issuance; a new credit facility (up to $50M) is meant to stop dilution.
Mine execution risk, mainly Copperstone.
TSXV micro-cap (~$110M).

PMVP.c1: Full. First-in-class reactivator of the p53 Y220C mutation (rezatapopt), a new cancer drug class.
PMVP.c2: Full. $3.50 base value vs $1.57: +123%, about 49%/yr over the default 2 years.
PMVP.c3: Partial (0.5). CEO Mack holds about 1.13M shares, about 1.5% (Yahoo insider roster).
PMVP.c4: Moderate (0.75). Patents and first-mover data in a defined mutation (46% ORR, 35/76; 10-month median duration of response). Not Strong because the data are single-arm, the mutation is rare, and resistance has already been seen.
PMVP.c5: Full. The warrant and dilution overhang is priced as failure, while the data point the other way; overreaction to financing, not data.
PMVP.c6: Full. Pivotal PYNNACLE readout in Q4 2026; NDA in Q1 2027.
flags: Runway about 6-7 quarters on ~$130M pro forma cash (under 24 months).
42M warrants at $1.21 plus pre-funded warrants: heavy dilution.
Single-asset, binary readout; ~$105M market cap.

HIMS.c1: Full. A vertically integrated direct-to-consumer telehealth platform (2.89M subscribers, Q2 revenue $753M), with a 2030 target of $6.5B revenue.
HIMS.c2: Zero. $41 fair value vs $29.81: +38% in total, under 25%/yr.
HIMS.c3: Full, with a caveat. Founder-CEO Andrew Dudum controls the company via super-voting Class V shares; Yahoo shows no direct-share figure. Without this credit, the score would be 3.75 and the stock would drop off the list.
HIMS.c4: Moderate (0.75). Brand, scale and vertical integration (pharmacy, fulfillment) plus an obsessive founder. Main threat: regulatory action (FDA on compounded peptides, FTC) and GLP-1 pricing from drugmakers.
HIMS.c5: Full. The stock fell about 15% on the FDA peptide committee and about 10% on the FTC suit; the author sizes the impact at about $3/share, so this is an overreaction.
HIMS.c6: Full. Wegovy list-price cut on Jan 1, 2027 and the FDA peptide decision.
flags: $1.0B of 2030 converts (convert price $70.67) plus $402.5M of 2032 converts at the money: ~6% dilution.
Gross margin down to ~64% from 76% a year ago.

NYXH.c1: Full. Genio implant for sleep apnea; if the label extends to complete concentric collapse (CCC) patients, it opens a large, growing market Nyxoah alone can serve.
NYXH.c2: Full. $11 DCF target vs $1.37: about 8x, far above 40%/yr even over the default 2 years.
NYXH.c3: Zero. The CEO is stepping down and isn't a large holder.
NYXH.c4: Moderate (0.75). Regulatory exclusivity in the CCC group plus the bilateral design and clinical data (77% responders in the CCC pivotal trial). Not Strong because the label isn't granted and Inspire could follow.
NYXH.c5: Full. Priced as post-dilution distress, not as a label-driven monopoly.
NYXH.c6: Full. FDA CCC label decision expected in early 2027.
flags: About EUR98M cash vs ~EUR18M/quarter burn; 166% dilution in 12 months, and the author models about 15% more.
EUR58M of debt.
CEO and CFO both leaving; a related-party deal with Man & Science; Inspire patent suits.
About $133M market cap; a binary FDA bet.

ELMT.c1: Full. The only US-owned, fully integrated tungsten and molybdenum producer, as defense supply chains move away from China.
ELMT.c2: Partial (0.5). $64-127 by 2031 vs $21.12: 3-6x over about 5 years, roughly 27-46%/yr (midpoint ~38%/yr).
ELMT.c3: Zero. The CEO's stake couldn't be verified.
ELMT.c4: Strong (1). Regulatory and strategic position: the only integrated domestic source, backed by a $450M Department of War commitment and a $2B-ceiling DLA IDIQ ($150M guaranteed). Main threat: execution on heavy capex.
ELMT.c5: Full. The market prices it as a small industrial; the author argues it is an irreplaceable Pentagon supplier.
ELMT.c6: Full. DFARS ban on Chinese tungsten effective Jan 1, 2027.
flags: DoW warrants: up to 19.9% dilution; heavy capex plan.
Strategic holder: US Department of War (warrants plus a board seat).

SHOE.c1: Partial (0.5). A cheap turnaround with little growth.
SHOE.c2: Full. More than 75% upside by end FY27 (about 1.3 years), above 40%/yr.
SHOE.c3: Partial (0.5). Returning CEO Sifford holds about 412K shares, about 1.5% (Yahoo).
SHOE.c4: Moderate (0.75). Edge: the returning CEO's proven 2012-21 record ($408M FCF, $194M buybacks). Main threat: a weak footwear retail backdrop.
SHOE.c5: Full. About 50% of the float is short after a ~45% EPS guidance cut; the author calls it an overreaction, with the stock priced below working capital.
SHOE.c6: Partial (0.5). Holiday-quarter and FY27 results; no specific dated event.
flags: Clean balance sheet: $132M cash, no debt, capex falling below $20M.
Guidance cut in Sept 2026 under the prior strategy.

ALM.long: SA beneficial long position in ALM / ALM:CA
ALM.c1: Full. Sangdong is framed as a long-life (21-year Plansee offtake with a price floor) non-China tungsten mine, so the thesis is secular supply security for tungsten, not a one-off trade.
ALM.c2: 0. Target $15.85 vs about $13.40 at publication through 2030 is roughly 17%/yr, under the 25%/yr bar.
ALM.c3: 0. CEO stake is not verified in the article.
ALM.c4: Moderate (0.75). Scarce non-China tungsten, a long offtake with a floor price, and a mine that is hard to replicate. Not Strong because the premium is still commodity-price risked and the company is early in first sales.
ALM.c5: Full. The market is pricing a tungsten-price crash that has not arrived; if the premium holds and Sangdong ramps, the author argues the stock is mispriced against his risked value.
ALM.c6: Full. First Sangdong sales expected mid-November (Q3), and DFARS non-China tungsten rules start 1 Jan 2027.
flags: Commodity-price risk: the author sizes it as a small, junior-style position.
CEO stake unverified.
Author target implies only ~17%/yr to 2030.
Thin notes reconstructed from full text.

GTLB.long: SA beneficial long position in GTLB
GTLB.c1: Full. AI coding and source-control sovereignty are treated as a multi-year secular shift that lifts GitLab’s addressable market versus GitHub.
GTLB.c2: 0. No explicit price target; the article is qualitative on upside.
GTLB.c3: 0. The CEO is not a large holder; the founder is chair.
GTLB.c4: Moderate (0.75). Product and reliability edge versus GitHub plus rising net ARR (+42% cited), but GitHub recovery and competition keep it from Strong.
GTLB.c5: Full. The market still treats GitHub as the default; the author argues reliability, sovereignty and AI-agent tooling will drive a 2027 inflection that the share price does not fully price.
GTLB.c6: Full. Orbit GA is next month and the 2027 inflection is dated within 24 months.
flags: Premium valuation already prices in strong execution.
GitHub recovery and rising competition are the main risks.
No own price target.
Thin notes reconstructed from full text.

KARO.c1: Full. Telematics / fleet SaaS with 15%+ end-market growth, ASEAN expansion and a durable South African franchise.
KARO.c2: 0. Thesis is "15-20% CAGR if the multiple holds"; no 40%/yr target.
KARO.c3: Full. Founder-CEO Isaias (Zack) Calisto is described as owning about two-thirds of the company.
KARO.c4: Moderate (0.75). ~40% South Africa share, 95% retention, net cash, no SBC and vertical integration. Not Strong because ASEAN is still early and Powerfleet / peers compete.
KARO.c5: Partial (0.5). The stock is called "expensive but underfollowed"; the differential is more about neglect than a clear temporary mispricing with a named correction path.
KARO.c6: Partial (0.5). Catalysts (ASEAN ramp, continued Rule-of-50 compounding) are not tightly dated within 24 months.

Concentration: ~70% of income from South Africa.
Thin notes reconstructed from full text.

SIRI.long: SA beneficial long position in SIRI
SIRI.c1: Partial (0.5). Framed mainly as a cheap, FCF-rich "living dead" asset (spectrum + satellite radio licence), not a long secular growth story.
SIRI.c2: Partial (0.5). $43 at 10x FCF now is about +62% (roughly 27%/yr over 2 years), or $64 after 3 years of buybacks (~36%/yr). Between 25 and 40%/yr.
SIRI.c3: 0. CEO is not a large holder.
SIRI.c4: Moderate (0.75). Only US satellite-radio licence plus spectrum that the author values above enterprise value; weakened streaming rivals help. Not Strong because the core audio business is mature.

SIRI.c6: Full. Share buybacks are guided to restart in 2027 after multi-year debt reduction.

Net debt was still material after the multi-year reduction cycle.

URGN.c2: 0. No own target; cites Street without a quantified 40%/yr path from the publish-day close.
URGN.c4: Moderate (0.75). RTGel delivery IP and first-mover status in non-surgical LG-IR-NMIBC. Not Strong because clinical competitors are coming.
